newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bankers agree to cut OTC dlr selling rate.
newsitem.headline: Manila bankers agree to cut OTC dlr selling rate.

text.p: The Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP) said on Tuesday banks would reduce their over-the-counter (OTC) dollar selling rates after a public outcry over the high rates amid uncertainties in the foreign exchange market.
Some banks were selling dollars as high as 35 pesos to a dollar to their clients when the peso was trading between 29 and 30 in the interbank market.
Individuals who need dollars of $5,000 or less primarily make up the OTC market.

"We've asked the members to narrow the band between buying and selling...There's a gentlemen's agreement (to cut the selling rate)," BAP president Deogracias Vistan told reporters after his meeting with bank presidents and treasurers.
He said banks had agreed to keep their selling rate below four percent of the previous day's weighted average.
"The free market must not be at the extreme prejudice of the public," Vistan added.
On Wednesday, the highest selling rate that can be offered to retail clients will be 30.80 pesos to the dollar, which is four-percent higher than Tuesday's average of 29.674.

Before the sharp peso depreciation, which was triggered by the de facto devaluation announced by the central bank last year, over-the-counter rates were just 30 to 50 centavos higher than the market rate.
The association is comprised of more than 50 commercial banks in the country.
